recipes.title: Pakistani Chicken Biryani
ingredients: 1 1/4 lb halal bone-in skinless chicken, cut up
1/4 cup neutral oil, plus more as needed
2 small Thai green chili peppers, chopped
1/2 tsp kosher salt for chicken sauce
1 tsp lemon juice for chicken sauce
Water for washing and soaking rice
recipes.instructions: Coat chicken with yogurt, marinade oil, biryani masala, ground spices, sugar and marinade salt; cover and refrigerate up to overnight. Wash and soak rice. Brown onions in oil and ghee for 20 minutes; deglaze. Add whole spices, garlic and ginger; fry 2 minutes. Add chicken; fry 3 minutes, then add tomato, chilies, plums and chicken water. Cover; simmer 30 minutes. Boil drained rice in rice water with salt, oil and lemon juice for 5 minutes; drain. Reduce chicken sauce 3 minutes; add sauce salt, garam masala, flakes, kewra and lemon juice. Layer rice around chicken with chaat masala, coloring mixed into milk, layering oil, herbs and lemon. Seal; heat medium 5 minutes, lowest 20 minutes; rest covered 10 minutes.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken and alcohol-free kewra essence. Check biryani masala, chaat masala and food coloring ingredients for halal suitability; the original recipe does not establish certification.
recipes.source_notes: First alternatives selected: homemade biryani masala, lemon juice rather than vinegar, ghee, sliced onions, Thai chilies, chaat masala, mint and milk. The referenced homemade masala formula was not supplied, so its composition is not invented. Numeric ingredient ranges use upper bounds; timed ranges use upper bounds except rice, whose stated target is 5 minutes with a 5-minute-30-second maximum. Optional chili flakes retained. Serving raitas and extra yogurt omitted as serving extras; optional additional coloring omitted. Water explicitly specified in the method is listed. Kewra is specified alcohol-free; the source ingredient list calls it essence while the method calls it water. Yield and listed prep/cook times preserved.

recipes.title: Pakistani Chicken Karahi
ingredients: 2.2 lb halal skinless bone-in chicken, cut into small pieces
1 tsp black peppercorns, freshly ground, plus more to taste
3 green chili peppers, slit in half
recipes.instructions: Heat ghee and oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Cook the onion for 6 minutes, until pale gold, then stir in garlic, crushed ginger and whole Serrano chilies for 1 minute. Add chicken and 1/2 tsp salt; fry for 5 minutes, until its surface changes color and released moisture subsides. Stir in tomatoes, coriander, cumin, chili powder and remaining salt for 1 minute. Cover and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring midway. Uncover; cook on high for 10 minutes until the sauce reduces and fat separates. Lower to medium, stir in yogurt for 3 minutes, then add black pepper and garam masala. Finish with slit chilies, julienned ginger and cilantro.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal skinless bone-in chicken. This adaptation retains ghee and plain yogurt and introduces no alcohol-containing sauce; publisher certification is not established by the original recipe.
recipes.source_notes: Numeric ranges use upper bounds. First alternatives chosen: neutral oil rather than additional ghee, Serrano rather than Thai chilies, and Roma rather than Vine tomatoes. Explicit spice and salt amounts retained rather than replacing them with to-taste quantities. The method's discretionary extra salt is not added. Serving breads and rice omitted as serving extras. Source yield and listed prep/cook times preserved; the individual source steps take longer than its stated 30-minute cook time.

recipes.title: Aloo Keema
ingredients: 1 large Russet potato, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
1/4 cup water, plus another 1/4 cup if dry
recipes.instructions: Heat grapeseed oil over medium-high heat. Add cinnamon, cumin seeds, cloves, coriander seeds, whole peppercorns and onion; brown for 10 minutes. Loosen the pan residue with the deglazing water. After it evaporates, cook garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Add beef, breaking it into small crumbs, and fry for 5 minutes until moisture evaporates. Stir in tomato, chilies, ground spices, salt and yogurt; fry for 5 minutes until the tomato softens and oil separates. Add potato and 1/4 cup water, adding the further 1/4 cup if dry. Cover over low-medium heat for 25 minutes, stirring midway. Reduce excess liquid over high heat if needed. Switch off; stir in garam masala, lemon juice and cilantro.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal ground beef. The retained plain whole-milk yogurt and spices require no alcohol substitution; halal meat sourcing is an adaptation assumption, not a publisher certification claim.
recipes.source_notes: Numeric ranges use upper bounds; the potato uses the large end of the stated size range. First alternatives chosen: grapeseed oil, lean beef, one large tomato and Serrano chilies. Optional coriander seeds and garam masala retained. Conditional extra water remains conditional rather than being added automatically. Deglazing water comes from the source method. Serving rice and breads omitted as serving extras. Source yield and prep/cook times preserved.

recipes.title: Chapli Kabab
ingredients: 1/2 large red onion, very finely chopped
2 green onions, white and green parts finely chopped
4 small Thai green chili peppers, finely chopped
1 tsp red chili flakes, plus more to taste
1 small Roma tomato, deseeded and very finely diced, excess pulp and juice discarded
Neutral oil for frying and shaping
1 tbsp corn flour (makai ka atta), only if needed for binding
recipes.instructions: Toast coriander, cumin and carom seeds over medium-low heat for 4 minutes. Add pomegranate seeds and pulse 5 times to a coarse mixture. Toast corn flour separately over medium heat for 5 minutes; cool. Combine beef, toasted ingredients, onion, scallions, chilies, garlic, ginger, measured cilantro, seasonings, egg and drained tomato. Knead with gloved hands for 4 minutes until cohesive and stringy; cover, refrigerating up to 24 hours. Heat generous oil in cast iron over high heat; cook a small seasoning tester. With oiled hands, portion heaped 1/4-cup patties, about 90 g. Press to 4.5 inches wide and at most 1/3 inch thick. Fry 2 minutes per side, spooning oil over, to 160°F/71°C. Drain; garnish. Add conditional flour if binding fails.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal ground beef with the source's 20% fat content and a suitable neutral frying oil. No animal fat or alcohol-containing condiment is added; the original recipe does not establish halal certification.
recipes.source_notes: Source yield is 10 chapli kababs; declared serving count is 5, assuming two kababs per serving for catalog purposes. Numeric ranges use upper bounds, including seed quantity, chili and garlic counts, ginger length, toast/knead/frying times and coarse-grinding pulses. Large onion size selected from medium-to-large. First alternatives chosen: corn flour rather than gram flour, Thai chilies, finely chopped garlic/ginger, hand kneading, and pressing patties in the pan. Optional carom seeds retained; tomato retained despite the method's 'if using' wording. Ground coriander and cilantro garnishes retained without invented quantities. Lemon wedges and optional raita omitted as serving extras. Conditional extra flour preserved separately. Source prep/cook times retained.

recipes.title: Pakistani Chicken Yakhni Pulao
ingredients: 2 3/4 cups water for broth, plus water as needed to restore strained broth volume
1 1/4 lb halal bone-in skinless chicken, cut up
1/2 small yellow onion, roughly chopped, for broth
1 cinnamon stick, 2 inches long, for broth
1 medium dried bay leaf for broth
1 medium dried bay leaf for pulao
1/2 tsp coriander seeds, roughly crushed, for pulao
1/2 tsp whole black peppercorns for pulao
1 cinnamon stick, 1 inch long, for pulao
2 small Thai green chili peppers, finely chopped
Water for washing and soaking rice
recipes.instructions: Combine broth water, chicken, broth onion, broth spices, green cardamom and broth salt; bring to a covered boil. Simmer gently, covered, 20 minutes. Remove chicken; strain out onion and spices, restoring broth to 2 3/4 cups with water. Wash and soak rice. Brown sliced onion in oil and ghee over medium heat for 12 minutes; deglaze. Add pulao whole spices, garlic and ginger; fry 2 minutes. Sear chicken over medium-high heat 3 minutes. Add pulao salt, chilies, tomato and yogurt; fry 3 minutes. Boil with broth; add drained rice and return to boiling. Partially cover; simmer medium 5 minutes. Seal tightly; cook lowest 15 minutes, rest covered 15 minutes. Finish with ground pepper, garam masala, cilantro and mint.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken for both the meat and homemade yakhni. No commercial stock or alcohol-containing sauce is needed. Ghee and plain yogurt are retained; publisher halal certification is not established by the original recipe.
recipes.source_notes: First alternatives chosen: ghee, crushed garlic and ginger, Thai chilies and chopped tomato; grapeseed oil and Roma tomato follow the source's named examples. Optional pulao cinnamon, black cardamom and tomato retained. Garlic count and timed ranges use upper bounds, including the 15-minute covered rest. Broth and pulao ingredients remain separate to preserve their different uses and the straining step. Deglazing and rice-washing water are explicitly supported by the method. Serving raitas and extra yogurt omitted as serving extras. Source yield and 80-minute cook time preserved. Prep time is blank because supplied prepTime is null; totalTime is 110 minutes, but a prep duration is not inferred.

recipes.title: Masoor Dal
ingredients: 1/4 cup neutral oil, such as grapeseed oil
1 small to medium yellow onion, finely chopped
1/4 cup water if lentils become too thick
recipes.instructions: Rinse lentils until the water clears, then drain. Bring lentils and 3 1/4 cups water to a boil; simmer with the lid ajar for 30 minutes, skimming and stirring occasionally. Add 1/4 cup water if thickening excessively. Separately, heat oil over medium-high heat. Fry cumin seeds for 15 seconds, onion for 7 minutes, then garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Add tomatoes, chili, ground cumin, coriander, chili powder, turmeric and salt; cook 3 minutes until softened and oil separates. Stir in lentils and 1 cup water, adjusting consistency. Simmer 5 minutes. Stir in ghee and optional crushed fenugreek. Off heat, add lemon juice, cilantro and optional garam masala.
recipes.halal_notes: Meat-free recipe containing ghee. Assumes plain ghee and spice blends without animal-derived or alcohol-containing additives; no publisher halal certification is asserted.
recipes.source_notes: Uses the first cooking method, stovetop, rather than Instant Pot. Selected first alternatives: Roma tomatoes, Thai chili, chopped chili preparation, red chili powder, sea salt and ghee. Kasuri methi and dried fenugreek leaves denote the same ingredient. Used upper bounds for garlic, chili powder and cilantro. Optional fenugreek and garam masala are retained. Method-only water additions are listed separately; rinse water is unmeasured. Serving extras are omitted. Publisher prep/cook times and four-serving yield are preserved, although the method also includes tempering and a final simmer.

recipes.title: Aloo Baingan
ingredients: 1 small to medium globe eggplant, unpeeled
1/2 cup neutral oil, divided between curry and pan-frying
Neutral oil as needed for additional pan-frying
2 medium russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
2 tbsp water if needed to soften tomatoes
recipes.instructions: Cut unpeeled eggplant into 1-inch cubes. Heat 1/4 cup oil over medium-high heat; fry eggplant in batches for 3 minutes per side, adding oil as needed. Set aside. Heat remaining measured oil; sizzle cumin seeds, then fry onion for 10 minutes. Deglaze with 2 tbsp water. Once dry, cook garlic and ginger for 1 minute. Add tomatoes, chili, ground spices and salt; cook 5 minutes, adding 2 tbsp water if needed. Fry potatoes in this masala for 3 minutes, add 1/2 cup water, cover and cook over low-medium heat for 10 minutes. Add eggplant; cook 17 minutes, using 1/4 cup water if sticking. If needed, sauté 3 minutes more. Finish off heat with cilantro, optional garam masala and lemon juice.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based ingredients. Assumes neutral vegetable oil and spice blends without animal-derived or alcohol-containing additives; no publisher halal certification is asserted.
recipes.source_notes: Selected first technique, pan-frying, instead of oven-roasting. The measured oil combines 1/4 cup for curry with the method's 1/4 cup for eggplant; additional frying oil remains unquantified. First alternatives selected: 2 medium tomatoes, Thai chili, kosher salt and optional garam masala. Upper bounds selected for garlic, chili powder, potato cube size and cooking-time ranges. Optional garam masala is retained. Method-only water is included with conditional additions identified. Bread serving extras are omitted. Source yield and prep/cook times are preserved.

recipes.title: Lebanese Mujadara
ingredients: 2 cups brown lentils, rinsed and drained
recipes.instructions: Cover the rice with cold soaking water and set aside. Heat olive oil in a large pot over high heat. Add sliced onions and stir constantly for about 20 minutes, until deeply browned with crisp edges. Lift onto paper towels, keeping the cooking oil. In another pot, bring lentils and 4 1/2 cups water to a boil. Cover tightly and cook over medium-low heat for 15 minutes. Drain and rinse the rice; add it and salt to the lentils. Stir once, cover and cook undisturbed for 15 minutes. Rest off heat, covered, for 5 minutes. Fork through the cumin, pour over the reserved oil and top with onions.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based recipe with olive oil and cumin; assumes plain ingredients without animal-derived or alcohol-containing additives.
recipes.source_notes: Selected the first rice alternative, long-grain white rice. Lebanese identity is explicit in the source title and description. Omitted cucumber yogurt sauce, which the method expressly makes an optional serving accompaniment; no sauce ingredients were supplied. Retained all onion cooking oil as directed. Unmeasured soaking water is separate from the 4 1/2 cups cooking water. Preserved source yield of eight servings and stated prep/cook times.

recipes.title: Shish Tawook
ingredients: 2 lb halal boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into large chunks
recipes.instructions: Whisk the plain whole-milk yogurt, lemon juice, olive oil and tomato paste in a large bowl. Mix in crushed garlic, paprika, cinnamon, oregano, ground ginger, salt and black pepper so the seasonings are evenly distributed. Add the large chicken chunks and turn them through the marinade until coated on all sides. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Just before cooking, thread the marinated chicken onto skewers. Grill over medium heat for 8 minutes per side, turning the skewers so both sides cook. Serve the grilled chicken warm.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken breast. Assumes plain yogurt, tomato paste and seasonings without animal-derived or alcohol-containing additives. Halal sourcing is an adaptation requirement, not a certification claimed by the publisher.
recipes.source_notes: Lebanese identity is explicit in the supplied description. Chicken is specified as halal; original cut and weight are unchanged. Used the upper bound of the source's 5–8 minutes per side. Omitted expressly optional onion wedges and pita bread, lettuce and garlic sauce serving extras. Preserved six-serving yield and stated prep/cook times; the separately required refrigeration period is at least four hours and is not included in the supplied prep time.

recipes.title: Lebanese Falafel
recipes.instructions: Cover dry chickpeas with water and soak at room temperature for 24 hours. Drain, rinse and dry thoroughly. Pulse chickpeas and salt in a food processor into fine, pebble-like pieces. Add parsley, cilantro, onion, garlic, cumin, coriander and black pepper; process into a thick paste, scraping the bowl as needed. Remove the blade, cover and refrigerate 1 hour. Gently fold in baking powder. Firmly shape 1 1/2-tbsp portions into balls. Heat oil 1 inch deep over medium heat until a little mixture sizzles. Fry batches of up to 12 without crowding, allowing 3 1/2 minutes per side until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towels and serve warm with tahini sauce.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based base recipe. Assumes vegetable frying oil and tahini sauce without animal-derived or alcohol-containing additives; the original recipe gives no tahini sauce formula or certification.
recipes.source_notes: Selected the first technique, frying, rather than alternative baking; baking-only cooking spray is therefore not included. Used upper bounds of 24 hours soaking, 12 balls per batch and 3 1/2 minutes frying per side, subject to avoiding crowding. Tahini sauce is retained without inventing its ingredients or quantity. Water is included from the soaking method. Source explicitly declares 18 servings, not 18 pieces; that serving count is preserved. Stated prep/cook times are retained and exclude the separately described soaking and one-hour refrigeration. Batch yield is 18 falafels; this catalog uses six servings of three falafels.

recipes.title: Lebanese Baba Ghanoush
recipes.instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Enclose the eggplant in aluminum foil and roast for 60 minutes, checking that a fork or knife enters the softened flesh easily. Open the foil and leave the eggplant to cool for 10 minutes. Once it is comfortable to handle, remove the stem end and peel away the skin, retaining the flesh. Transfer the flesh to a food processor or blender with the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt. Process in short pulses until everything is combined, stopping while the dip still has a chunky texture.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based ingredients; assume tahini contains no alcohol-containing additions.
recipes.source_notes: Selected the upper bounds of 3–4 tablespoons lemon juice and 45–60 minutes roasting. Source cookTime is retained as 45 minutes despite the longer selected roasting time. Omitted serving extras: olive oil, pomegranate seeds and pita chips.

recipes.title: Lebanese Rice with Vermicelli
ingredients: ½ cup dried rice vermicelli noodles
recipes.instructions: Wash the rice under cold water until the runoff is clear, then drain thoroughly. Warm the olive oil in a medium nonstick pot over medium heat. Add the dried vermicelli and stir frequently as it turns a deep golden brown, watching closely to prevent burning. Stir in the drained rice so it mixes with the noodles and becomes coated in oil. Add the salt and optional cinnamon. Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Remove from the heat, leave covered for 5 minutes, then uncover and fluff with a fork.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based recipe; assume the packaged rice vermicelli contains no alcohol-containing additions.
recipes.source_notes: Added the 4 cups water explicitly specified in the method. Retained optional cinnamon. Omitted optional parsley garnish and toasted nuts serving extra. Source prepTime is unspecified. Based only on original recipe.

recipes.title: Chicken Shawarma Pitas
ingredients: ⅓ cup extra virgin olive oil
recipes.instructions: Combine the cumin, turmeric, coriander, garlic powder, paprika, cloves and cayenne. Pat the chicken dry, salt both sides and cut into thin bite-sized pieces. Toss with the spices, onion, lemon juice and olive oil, then cover and refrigerate for 3 hours. Heat the oven to 425°F and let the chicken stand outside the refrigerator for a few minutes. Lightly oil a sheet pan with some of the measured oil and spread the chicken and onion in one layer. Roast for 30 minutes; optionally broil on the top rack for up to 1 minute, watching closely. Fill the pitas with tahini sauce, chicken and arugula.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken thighs and tahini sauce made without alcohol-containing ingredients. Assume the prepared salad and pita contain no prohibited additions; the publisher is not represented as certifying them.
recipes.source_notes: Yield is 6 shawarma pitas; declared 6 servings at one pita each. Chose tahini sauce over tzatziki and 3-hour marination over overnight, taking the first alternatives. Omitted optional pickles or olives. Retained sauce and salad as prepared components because their linked recipes were not supplied; no component ingredients invented. Used sweet paprika as specified in the method and included listed cayenne in the spice mixture. Reserved some measured oil for the pan because its additional oil amount is unspecified. Preserved supplied Middle Eastern cuisine label because no narrower tradition is identified. Prep and cook fields exclude the stated marination. Based only on original recipe. The separate linked cucumber-tomato salad is omitted; tahini sauce remains a prepared condiment.

recipes.title: Shakshuka
ingredients: Red pepper flakes, optional, a pinch
¼ cup chopped fresh parsley leaves
¼ cup chopped fresh mint leaves
recipes.instructions: Warm the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion, green peppers, garlic, coriander, paprika, cumin, optional red pepper flakes, salt and black pepper. Stir occasionally for about 5 minutes, until the vegetables soften. Add the chopped tomatoes and tomato sauce. Cover and simmer for about 15 minutes, then uncover and continue cooking until the sauce thickens. Taste and adjust the seasoning. Make six spaced hollows in the sauce and carefully crack one egg into each. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover and cook gently until the whites set. Uncover and scatter over the parsley and mint.
recipes.halal_notes: Meat-free egg dish; assume packaged tomato sauce contains no alcohol-containing ingredients.
recipes.source_notes: Used the explicitly supplied Tunisian cuisine label. Retained optional red pepper flakes and both herbs. Omitted bread serving extras. Source yield is up to 6 people; declared 6 servings. Preserved prepTime and cookTime despite the source totalTime inconsistency. Based only on original recipe.

recipes.title: Moroccan Harira
ingredients: 7 cups vegetable stock, preferably low-sodium, plus more as needed
¼ cup uncooked long grain rice, rinsed
recipes.instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, carrot and salt; stir regularly for 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and spices and cook for 2 minutes. Add the crushed tomatoes, tomato paste, cilantro, both lentils and chickpeas. Season with salt and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes. Pour in the vegetable stock, bring to a boil and boil for 5 minutes. Reduce to low, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until the legumes are very tender. Add more stock as needed to keep the soup pourable. Stir in the rice and cook for another 15 minutes, until cooked.
recipes.halal_notes: Selected vegetable stock rather than chicken stock; use stock without alcohol-containing ingredients. The resulting recipe is plant-based, assuming plain canned legumes and tomatoes.
recipes.source_notes: Selected first alternatives: vegetable stock rather than chicken stock, long grain rice rather than broken vermicelli, and additional stock rather than water. Used the method's explicit 4 tablespoons oil. Selected 2 minutes from the 1–2 minute garlic cooking range. Omitted lemon wedges as a serving extra. Source yield is up to 6 people; declared 6 servings. Retained source cookTime of 45 minutes, although the sequential method takes longer. The final rice step says 'another 15' without a unit; interpreted as minutes in cooking context. Based only on original recipe.

recipes.title: Fattoush Salad
ingredients: 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, for frying
2 tsp sumac, for pita and finishing
5 green onions, white and green parts chopped
1/3 cup extra virgin olive oil, for dressing
recipes.instructions: Tear the pitas into small pieces. Heat 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, then fry the bread, turning often, until browned and crisp. Drain on paper towels and season with some salt, pepper and the 2 teaspoons sumac, reserving some sumac for finishing. Put the lettuce, cucumber, tomatoes, green onions, radishes and parsley in a large bowl. Whisk the lemon juice with the dressing oil, salt, pepper, dressing sumac, cinnamon and allspice. Toss the vegetables gently with this dressing. Fold in the crisp pita just before serving and finish with the reserved sumac.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based with the optional molasses omitted. Check packaged pita ingredients for suitability; no publisher halal certification is implied.
recipes.source_notes: Its cuisine label is Middle Eastern; a more specific national attribution was not supplied. Chose lemon over lime and chopped cucumber over half-moons. Omitted explicitly optional mint and pomegranate molasses. Frying oil quantity comes from the method. Unmeasured salt listings are represented once. Additional discretionary sumac is not quantified. No cook time was supplied.

recipes.title: Tabouli Salad
ingredients: 4 firm Roma tomatoes, very finely chopped
2 bunches fresh parsley, partly stemmed and very finely chopped
15 fresh mint leaves, stemmed and very finely chopped
4 green onions, white and green parts very finely chopped
recipes.instructions: Rinse the fine bulgur, cover with water and soak for 7 minutes. Drain it thoroughly, squeezing out the remaining moisture by hand. Wash and dry the parsley and mint well before chopping them very finely. Finely chop the cucumber and green onions, keeping both onion colors. Chop the tomatoes equally finely and leave them in a colander so excess juice drains away. Combine the drained tomatoes, cucumber, herbs and onions with the bulgur. Season with salt and fold gently together. Add the lime juice and olive oil, mix again, then cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes before transferring to a serving dish.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based. Check the packaged bulgur and olive oil ingredients for suitability; no publisher halal certification is assumed.
recipes.source_notes: Based only on the original recipe, which labels the cuisine Middle Eastern without a specific national attribution. Chose lime juice rather than lemon. Used upper bounds for mint, juice, oil and the 5–7-minute soak. Yield is listed both as 6 and 6–8; declared 8 servings using the range's upper bound. No cook time was supplied.

recipes.title: Spanakorizo (Greek Spinach Rice)
recipes.instructions: Rinse the rice repeatedly until the runoff is clear. Cover it with water by an inch and soak for 20 minutes, or until a grain breaks easily between your fingers. Heat the olive oil in a braising pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden. Add spinach, lemon juice, garlic, tomato paste, salt and pepper; stir until the spinach wilts, then add mint and dill. Drain the rice and stir it in with the warm water. Boil for 3 minutes, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes until tender and dry. Rest covered for 10 minutes, then fluff.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based after omitting the feta garnish. Check packaged tomato paste ingredients for suitability; no cheese certification is assumed.
recipes.source_notes: Preserved publisher yield of 6 servings. Omitted optional feta, additional spinach and parsley garnishes. Selected 10 minutes, the upper bound of the 5–10-minute covered rest. recipes.title: Chana Masala
ingredients: 1 cup water, for gravy, plus more as needed
3/4 tsp salt, plus more to taste
2 tbsp fresh coriander leaves, finely chopped
recipes.instructions: Rinse chickpeas three times, soak in 4 cups water for at least 8 hours, then drain and rinse. Pressure-cook with 1 1/2 cups water for 6 whistles; let pressure fall naturally and check they mash easily. Heat oil; sizzle bay, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom. Fry onions and chili until lightly golden, then stir in ginger garlic paste for 1 minute. Cook tomatoes and salt until thick and pulpy. Add powdered spices except mango powder; fry for 4 minutes. Blend the cooled masala, removing bay, chili and cinnamon first. Return it to the pan with chickpeas, 1 1/4 cups chickpea cooking liquid and 1 cup water, adding water as needed. Cover, simmer 15 minutes, then add mango powder, fenugreek and coriander leaves.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based; use ginger garlic paste and spice blends without alcohol or animal-derived additives. Cooking liquid is from the chickpeas, not meat stock. No publisher halal certification is implied.
recipes.source_notes: Selected dried raw chickpeas, ginger garlic paste and fresh chopped tomatoes as the first ingredient alternatives. Retained all listed optional spices and chili. Selected upper bounds for soaking water, pressure-cooker whistles, paste, spice-frying time and additional gravy water. Used the source's optional smooth-masala technique without its optional added chickpeas. Reused 1 1/4 cups chickpea cooking liquid rather than counting it as another purchased ingredient; additional water remains as needed. Omitted discretionary lemon juice and suggested serving accompaniments. Publisher prep/cook times exclude the separately stated overnight or minimum 8-hour soak. Cinnamon length remains explicit without inventing a weight or count.

recipes.title: Palak Paneer
ingredients: 150 g microbial/vegetarian-rennet or halal-certified paneer (1 1/4 cups)
90 g onion, finely chopped (3/4 cup; 1 small)
1/2 cup tomato, deseeded and chopped (1 small)
Water, for rinsing and adjusting consistency as needed
recipes.instructions: Remove tough spinach stems, rinse the tender leaves thoroughly and drain well. Heat 1/2 tablespoon oil and sauté the chilies, cashews and spinach for 4 minutes until wilted. Cool completely, then blend smoothly with 1/4 cup water. Heat the remaining oil and sizzle the cumin, cardamom, cinnamon and cloves. Fry onion until translucent to golden; add ginger garlic paste and cook 2 minutes. Add tomato and salt, cooking until mushy, then fry garam masala for 2 minutes. Add 3/4 cup water, cover and cook until onion softens. On low heat, add fenugreek and spinach purée; cook 3 minutes until bubbling. Adjust with water if necessary, fold in paneer and turn off the heat.
recipes.halal_notes: Specify microbial/vegetarian-rennet or halal-certified paneer and check its ingredients; the publisher does not establish its certification. Use oil and check ginger garlic paste and garam masala for unsuitable additives.
recipes.source_notes: Selected the first ingredient alternatives: all oil and chopped tomato; selected sautéing rather than blanching the spinach. The method's butter mixture was reconciled with the ingredient list's explicit all-oil option by using the remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons oil for gravy. Omitted optional cream garnish and suggested serving accompaniments; retained optional whole spices and fenugreek. Used upper bounds for spinach, cashews, garam masala and stated cooking-time ranges. Yield is listed as both 2 and 2–3; declared 3 servings using the range's upper bound. Paneer sourcing is the halal adaptation. Additional water is discretionary, not assigned a fixed quantity. Cinnamon length is preserved without conversion.

recipes.title: Dal Tadka
ingredients: 200 g dried split pigeon pea, 1 cup (200 g) dry toor dal (split pigeon peas)
¾ cup hot water, only if needed to adjust consistency
½ tsp cumin seeds, for the dal base
1 tsp ginger (1 inch), peeled and finely chopped
2 medium tomatoes (1 cup), deseeded and finely chopped
¾ tsp red chilli powder, for the dal base
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
¾ tsp cumin seeds, for tempering
1 tbsp garlic, finely chopped, for tempering
⅓ tsp red chilli powder, for tempering
recipes.instructions: Rinse and drain the dal. Add 3 cups water and pressure-cook over medium heat for 4 whistles; let pressure fall naturally, then mash lightly. Use hot water only if needed. Heat oil, crackle the base cumin, and gently fry ginger and garlic. Add onion and green chilli; cook until lightly golden. Briefly stir in turmeric, base chilli powder and garam masala, then soften tomatoes with salt. Combine with dal and simmer 7 minutes. Stir in fenugreek and coriander. Separately heat ghee; crackle remaining cumin and mustard. Add dried chillies, garlic and curry leaves without browning. Stir in asafoetida and remaining chilli powder, remove from heat and pour over dal. Serve with lemon.
recipes.halal_notes: Meat-free preparation using ghee. Assumes pure dairy ghee and spice blends or compounded asafoetida without alcohol or non-halal additives; no publisher certification is implied.

recipes.title: Vegetable Biryani
ingredients: ½ cup onion (1 medium), thinly sliced
¼ tsp salt, for cooking water
recipes.instructions: Soak rice for at least 20 minutes, then drain. Heat oil in a heavy pot and fry bay leaf, star anise, shahi jeera, cloves, cardamom and cinnamon for 2 minutes. Brown onion with green chilli, then cook ginger garlic paste for 1 minute. Fry potato, carrot and peas for 2 minutes. Add tomato, vegetable salt, curd, herbs and ground spices; cook over high heat for 3 minutes until tomato softens. Lower heat and spread rice over the vegetables. Boil the water with its salt and pour around the edges without stirring. Bring to a rolling boil, cover and cook over low-medium heat until absorbed and cooked. Rest off heat for 15 minutes, then fluff.
recipes.halal_notes: Meat-free recipe using oil and curd. Assumes plain curd and packaged spice blends or ginger garlic paste without alcohol or non-halal additives; no certification is asserted.

recipes.title: Paneer Tikka Masala
ingredients: 250 g halal-certified paneer, cut into 1-inch cubes
1 tsp ginger garlic paste, for marinade
½ tsp Kashmiri red chilli powder, for marinade
½ tsp garam masala, for marinade
¼ tsp dried fenugreek leaves, for marinade
½ small onion, diced and layers separated (optional)
2 tbsp oil, for sauce, divided equally
1½ tsp ginger garlic paste, for sauce
1 tsp red chilli powder, less spicy kind, for sauce
¾ cup water, for cooking sauce
1 tsp dried fenugreek leaves, for sauce (optional)
recipes.instructions: Coat paneer, pepper and separated onion layers with hung curd, marinade ginger garlic paste, Kashmiri chilli, garam masala, fenugreek, turmeric, salt, lemon and oil. Set aside. In half the sauce oil, soften cubed onion; add tomatoes, cashews, sugar and sauce salt. Once soft, fry sauce chilli powder and garam masala for 2 minutes. Cool, then blend with ¾ cup water. Sizzle whole spices in remaining oil; fry remaining paste for 2 minutes. Add puree and cooking water; cover and simmer 10 minutes, stirring. Add sauce fenugreek. Preheat oven to 220°C for 15 minutes. Skewer marinated ingredients; grill 10 minutes, turning after 5. Fold into sauce with cream and finish with coriander.
recipes.halal_notes: Specify halal-certified paneer; this is an adaptation requirement, not a claim about the publisher's cheese. Assumes plain hung curd, cream and packaged spice or paste ingredients without alcohol or non-halal additives.

Paneer sourcing adapted as explained in halal_notes. Suggested breads and rice omitted. Source yield is 4 servings.

recipes.title: Punjabi Rajma Masala
ingredients: 200 g dried kidney bean, 1 cup (200 g) dry kidney beans
4 cups water, for soaking and discarding
1 cup hot water, only if needed for gravy
120 g onion, 1 cup (120 g) onion, finely chopped
1½ cups tomatoes (2 large, 300 g), chopped and pureed
¾ tsp garam masala, for the sauce
½ tsp garam masala, reserved for adjustment if needed
½ tsp additional salt, only if needed
recipes.instructions: Rinse kidney beans three times. Soak uncovered in 4 cups water for at least 6 hours or overnight, then discard soaking water and rinse. Pressure-cook with 1½ cups fresh water for 5 whistles, until beans mash easily while holding their shape. Heat ghee; sizzle bay leaf and cumin seeds. Fry onion and green chilli over medium heat until golden, then ginger garlic paste for 1 minute. Add pureed tomatoes and thicken for 3 minutes. Fry the sauce garam masala and other ground spices for 3 minutes. Add beans, cooking liquid and hot water only as needed; simmer 15 minutes. Add salt, fenugreek, reserved seasoning if needed, cream, coriander and ginger.
recipes.halal_notes: Meat-free bean curry using ghee and optional dairy cream. Assumes pure dairy products and spice blends or ginger garlic paste without alcohol or non-halal additives; bean cooking liquid is the stock.
recipes.source_notes: Selected first alternatives: dry kidney beans, ghee, finely chopped onion, ginger garlic paste, fresh tomatoes and Kashmiri chilli powder. recipes.title: Aloo Gobi
ingredients: 1½ cups potatoes (2 medium), cut into ¾-inch cubes
180 g cauliflower floret, 2 cups (180 g) cauliflower florets, cut to 1½ inches
½ tbsp ginger (½ inch), peeled and minced
½ tbsp garlic (4 cloves), peeled and minced
Water, as needed for soaking, rinsing and an optional cooking splash
recipes.instructions: Soak cauliflower in slightly hot water for 4 minutes, then rinse and drain thoroughly. Keep potato cubes in water until needed. Heat oil and crackle cumin seeds; fry ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then onion until translucent. Add drained potatoes and green chilli; stir-fry 3 minutes. Cover over low-medium heat until half-cooked, adding a splash of water if needed. Add cauliflower and fry 3 minutes. Mix in ground spices and 3 tablespoons water. Cover, stirring occasionally, until nearly tender; add salt and finish cooking potatoes while keeping cauliflower slightly firm. Add tomatoes and fenugreek; fry over medium-high heat for 4 minutes. Finish with mango powder, coriander and optional lemon juice.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based preparation. Assumes oil and packaged spice blends contain no alcohol or non-halal additives; no certification is claimed.
recipes.source_notes: First alternatives selected: cubed potatoes, fresh chopped tomatoes, minced ginger and minced garlic, and slit green chilli. recipes.title: Masala Dosa
ingredients: ¾ tsp pink salt for batter
¾ cup water for blending rice
2 cups cubed potatoes (source also gives 500 g or 3 medium)
1 tsp skinned urad dal for filling
Water as needed for rinsing, soaking, boiling and adjusting batter
Oil as needed for cooking dosas
recipes.instructions: Soak rinsed dals, fenugreek and rice separately for 5 hours; soak poha for 30 minutes. Drain. Blend batter dals, fenugreek and poha with 1¼ cups water and pink salt; blend rice with ¾ cup water. Combine; ferment warmly until risen, up to 16 hours. Boil potatoes until just tender. Soak filling dals 30 minutes; drain. Fry cumin, mustard and filling dals in oil until golden. Add onions, curry leaves and chilies; brown lightly. Fry asafoetida and ginger, then add crumbled potatoes, turmeric, salt and filling water. Cook 3 minutes; add coriander. Spread pourable batter thinly on a medium-hot griddle; drizzle oil. Cook until edges release, flip for 1 minute, then crisp the underside. Fill and fold.
recipes.halal_notes: Meat-free batter and potato filling; assumes butter and packaged asafoetida contain no non-halal additives.
recipes.source_notes: Source yield is 20 dosas; declared as 10 servings of 2 dosas. First ingredient alternatives selected, including sona masuri rice, pink salt and grated ginger. Butter retained as listed; the method's oil alternative is used for cooking. Additional water and cooking oil are explicitly mentioned in the source method. recipes.title: Mushroom Masala Curry
ingredients: 300 g mushrooms, stems trimmed and quartered
120 g onion, 1 cup finely chopped onion (120 g)
280 g fresh tomato puree, 1¼ cups fresh tomato puree (280 g)
¾ cup hot water for gravy
¼ cup hot water for cashews
Water as needed to thin gravy
recipes.instructions: Soak cashews in ¼ cup hot water, then puree smoothly. Heat 2½ tablespoons oil with bay leaf, cumin seeds, cardamom and cinnamon. Add onion and fry for 10 minutes until golden. Stir in ginger and garlic for 1 minute; loosen the pan with 2 tablespoons water. Add ground spices and salt, then tomato puree; reduce until thick and aromatic. Stir in cashew puree and ¾ cup hot water. Bring to a vigorous boil, then cover and simmer until the onion softens and gravy thickens. Fry mushrooms separately in remaining oil for 5 minutes; add to gravy. Cover until tender, thinning if needed. Finish with fenugreek, lemon juice and coriander; add sugar only if tart.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based version using oil and cashews; assumes packaged spice blends contain no non-halal additives.

recipes.title: Bhindi Masala
recipes.instructions: Rinse okra, dry it completely, trim both ends and cut into ¾-inch lengths. Heat 1½ tablespoons oil over medium heat. Fry okra for 7 minutes, stirring frequently, until partly cooked and no longer sticky; set aside. Heat remaining oil in the same pan and let cumin seeds splutter. Add onion and slit chili; fry until golden. Cook ginger garlic paste for 2 minutes, then add tomatoes and salt and soften thoroughly. Stir in turmeric, chili powder, garam masala and ground coriander; fry until the masala pulls away from the pan. Add 6 tablespoons water and reduce until thick. Mix in fenugreek and okra. Cover over low heat until tender, then uncover to evaporate moisture. Finish with coriander leaves.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based recipe; assumes the ginger garlic paste and spice blends contain no non-halal additives.
recipes.source_notes: First alternatives selected for onion preparation, ginger garlic paste and chopped tomatoes. Upper bounds selected for chili powder, garam masala and cooking ranges. Method supplies 6 tbsp water; additional water remains as needed. Optional seasonings and coriander retained. Serving rice and breads omitted.

recipes.title: Indian Chicken Curry
ingredients: ½ tsp additional garam masala if needed
recipes.instructions: Heat oil over medium heat in a deep pan. Add bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom, followed by onions and chilies. Fry for 8 minutes until deeply golden. Cook ginger garlic paste for 1 minute. Add tomatoes, turmeric and salt; cook until the tomatoes collapse. Lower heat and stir in yogurt, chili powder, 1 teaspoon garam masala and ground coriander; cook until aromatic. Add chicken and coriander leaves; fry over medium heat for about 3 minutes until pale. Cover on low heat for 4 minutes. Pour in hot water gradually, starting with ½ cup. Cover and cook over medium heat until chicken is fully cooked and tender and gravy thickens. Add the extra garam masala if needed.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken. Assumes plain yogurt, ginger garlic paste and spice blends contain no non-halal additives; publisher certification is not asserted.

recipes.title: Malaysian Chicken Satay
ingredients: 2 lb halal boneless skinless chicken breast
recipes.instructions: Cut the halal chicken breast into small cubes and set aside while preparing the marinade. Put cooking oil, the white parts of the lemongrass, peeled garlic, shallots, turmeric, coriander, chili powder, salt and sugar into a food processor. Blend into a marinade, adding a little water only if needed. Coat the chicken thoroughly, then refrigerate for 6 hours. Thread 4 pieces onto each bamboo skewer. Grill for 3 minutes per side, brushing with basting oil during cooking, until the chicken is fully cooked and the surfaces are charred. Serve the skewers hot alongside the cucumber pieces and quartered onion.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal boneless, skinless chicken breast. Assumes cooking oil and ground spices contain no non-halal additives. No certification is attributed to the publisher.

recipes.title: Beef Rendang
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb halal boneless beef short ribs, cubed
1 lemongrass stalk, cut into 4-inch lengths and pounded
2 tsp tamarind pulp, soaked in warm water and strained
6 kaffir lime leaves, very finely sliced
12 dried chilies, soaked in warm water and seeded
recipes.instructions: Finely blend the shallots, galangal, white lemongrass parts, garlic, ginger and soaked, seeded chilies. Heat the oil in a stew pot; fry this paste with cinnamon, cloves, star anise and cardamom until fragrant. Stir in the beef and pounded lemongrass for 1 minute. Add coconut milk, strained tamarind soaking liquid and the measured water. Simmer over medium heat, stirring often, until the beef is nearly cooked. Mix in the lime leaves, kerisik and sugar. Cover and cook over low heat for 1 1/2 hours, until the beef is very tender and the sauce has reduced and clings to it. Season with salt.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal beef short ribs. Assume plain coconut milk and toasted coconut without alcohol-containing additives; check packaged ingredients.

recipes.title: Nasi Lemak
ingredients: 3 pandan leaves, tied into a knot
Tamarind pulp, the size of a small ping-pong ball
Salt to taste for sambal and fish
1 red onion, peeled and sliced into rings
recipes.instructions: Rinse and drain the rice, then cook with its water, coconut milk, measured salt and pandan; discard the leaves. Pound shallots, garlic, chilies and belacan into a paste. Soak tamarind in its water for 15 minutes, squeezing it, then strain. Rinse and drain anchovies; fry in the oil until pale brown and crisp, then drain. Transfer 2 tablespoons of that oil to a pan. Fry the paste over medium-low heat until fragrant and reddish. Add onion rings, anchovies, tamarind liquid, sugar and salt; simmer gently until thick. Salt the sardines and deep-fry in the remaining oil. Plate the rice with sambal, fish, eggs, peanuts and cucumber.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal-certified belacan; this is an adaptation requirement, not a publisher certification claim. Use plain dried anchovies and halal-appropriate sardines, and check packaged condiments for alcohol-containing additives.

Tamarind size is preserved without a weight conversion. No ingredients omitted.

recipes.title: Roti Canai
ingredients: 420 g all-purpose flour, 3 1/2 cups all-purpose flour (420 g; source also lists 14.8 oz)
recipes.instructions: Mix flour, salt, sugar and 1/4 cup ghee with a dough hook on low until clumpy. Add egg, milk and water; knead for 10 minutes until soft and elastic. Divide into eight balls. Coat each with 1 teaspoon ghee, cover with a damp cloth and rest at room temperature for at least 6 hours. Bring chilled dough to room temperature before shaping. Grease hands and the work surface with remaining ghee. Stretch each ball into a paper-thin sheet about 2 feet across; fold inward from each side to trap air in an 8-inch layered square. Flatten to 8 inches. Cook on a lightly ghee-greased griddle over low heat for 4 minutes per side until golden. Carefully clap the hot breads to loosen their layers.
recipes.halal_notes: This meat-free recipe uses egg, milk and ghee. Assume plain dairy ghee without animal-fat blends or alcohol-containing additives; check its label.
recipes.source_notes: Source yield is 8 pieces; declared as 4 servings of 2 pieces. Source prep and cook metadata are retained; the method additionally requires at least 6 hours of resting. recipes.title: Malaysian Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 oz curry powder for meat (source also lists 30 g)
2 small Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into wedges
recipes.instructions: Heat the oil in a pot and cook the diced onion until softened and fragrant. Add the meat curry powder and stir promptly so its aroma develops without letting it sit on the hot base. Add the chicken thighs, turning them through the onion and spices for about 1 minute. Pour in the water and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, add potato wedges and the optional tomato and eggs, then cover. Simmer gently for about 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender. If the sauce remains thin, continue simmering until it thickens. Stir in the coconut cream and salt, mixing thoroughly before serving hot.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken thighs. Assume the meat curry powder is a spice blend without non-halal meat derivatives; check its ingredients and the coconut cream label.

recipes.title: Ayam Masak Merah
ingredients: 2 kg halal chicken, cut into pieces (source suggests 2 chickens, each cut into 8 pieces)
1/4 cup vegetable oil for the spice paste
recipes.instructions: Coat the chicken with turmeric and salt and leave for 30 minutes. Heat vegetable oil in a wok and deep-fry the pieces until golden; set aside. Roughly chop the onions, ginger, galangal and lemongrass, then blend with soaked chilies and garlic into a paste. Heat the measured oil in the wok and fry cinnamon, star anise, ground cloves and cardamom until aromatic. Add the paste and raise the heat until bubbling. Reduce the heat and cook until fragrant and oil separates from the paste. Add tomato soup, coconut milk and chicken. Bring briefly to a boil, then simmer until the sauce thickens. Adjust salt to taste.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken. Choose alcohol-free tomato soup with vegetable stock or halal-certified animal-derived ingredients; no publisher certification is implied. Check coconut milk and packaged spices for suitable ingredients.

recipes.title: Tandoori Chicken
recipes.instructions: Pat the chicken legs dry. Stir together the yogurt, ginger, garlic, garam masala, cayenne, lime juice, measured oil, salt and turmeric. Coat the chicken thoroughly and marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably 4 hours. Heat the oven to 400°F. Set a wire rack over a foil-lined baking sheet and arrange the chicken on it. Bake for 20 minutes, turn the legs, then bake for another 20 minutes. Brush both sides with basting oil a couple of times during baking. Broil for 1 minute, until lightly charred, and serve immediately with the lime wedges.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken legs and plain Greek yogurt with suitable ingredients. Halal sourcing is an adaptation requirement, not a publisher certification.
recipes.source_notes: Retained the stated 3-person yield. Optional red coloring omitted; optional salt retained at the stated amount rather than the to-taste alternative. recipes.title: Garlic Butter Salmon Kebabs
recipes.instructions: Cut the salmon into cubes approximately 1 inch across and place in a bowl. Add the olive oil, salt and ground black pepper, then turn the pieces to coat them evenly. Thread three salmon cubes onto each skewer. In a separate bowl, combine the minced garlic with the melted salted butter, lemon juice and chopped parsley, stirring until evenly mixed. Preheat the grill. Grill the skewers for about 2 minutes on each side, until the salmon is cooked through. Move the kebabs onto a platter, spoon the garlic butter mixture over them and serve immediately.
recipes.halal_notes: Use salmon suitable for the household's halal requirements and salted butter with suitable ingredients. No alcohol-containing sauce is included; publisher certification is not asserted.

recipes.title: Thai Green Chicken Curry
ingredients: 8 oz halal chicken breast, cut into bite-sized pieces
2 red chilies, cut into thick strips
recipes.instructions: Warm the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the green curry paste and stir as it fries until fragrant. Put in the chicken pieces and mix thoroughly so the paste coats them. Pour in the coconut milk and water, then bring briefly to a boil. Add the bamboo shoots, bruised lime leaves and strips of red chili. Reduce the heat, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until the sauce has thickened slightly and the chicken is cooked through. Stir in the fish sauce, sugar and Thai basil leaves. Remove the pot from the heat and serve immediately.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken breast. Check green curry paste, including any shrimp paste it contains, and fish sauce for halal certification; use alcohol-free fish sauce. These are sourcing requirements, not verified product or publisher certifications.
recipes.source_notes: Selected sugar, the first alternative, rather than palm sugar. recipes.title: Hummus
ingredients: 400 g canned chickpeas (1 can), drained; reserve liquid and about 10 chickpeas
1/4 cup liquid from the canned chickpeas
1/4 tsp cooking salt, plus more to taste
Extra virgin olive oil for topping
recipes.instructions: Drain the chickpeas, saving their liquid and setting aside about 10 chickpeas for the topping. Stir the tahini well before measuring it. Place the remaining chickpeas in a food processor with the minced garlic, fresh lemon juice, tahini and measured olive oil. Process into a paste, then add the cooking salt and black pepper. Pour in the measured chickpea liquid and blend for a couple of minutes until smooth and soft enough to drop from a spoon. Adjust the salt as needed. Spread in a shallow bowl, make swirls with a spoon, and finish with the reserved chickpeas, topping oil and paprika.
recipes.halal_notes: Plant-based ingredients; check packaged tahini and canned chickpeas for suitable ingredients. No publisher halal certification is asserted.

recipes.title: Malaysian Satay Chicken Curry
ingredients: 1 1/4 tsp chilli powder, not US chili seasoning
750 g halal chicken thigh fillets, cut into bite-sized pieces
3/4 cup roasted unsalted peanuts, chopped and divided
3 tsp alcohol-free halal-certified dark soy sauce
recipes.instructions: Mix the spices, salt and sugar. Marinate chicken with grated onion and 3 1/2 tbsp seasoning for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight; the source allows 20 minutes minimum. Brown chicken in two batches over high heat using 1 tbsp oil; reserve. At medium heat, soften chilies, diced onion and garlic in remaining oil for 2 minutes. Fry remaining seasoning for 1 minute. Blend with broth and 1/2 cup peanuts; return to skillet. Stir in remaining peanuts, kecap manis, soy sauce, coconut milk and peanut butter. Add bruised lime leaves and chicken. Simmer over medium-low heat for 15 minutes until thickened and chicken is cooked through. Stir in lime juice.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken thigh fillets and halal chicken broth. Source alcohol-free halal-certified kecap manis and dark soy sauce; no specific product certification has been verified. Check packaged curry powder and peanut butter ingredients. These requirements do not imply publisher certification.
recipes.source_notes: Selected 6 servings from the displayed 5–6 range and 6 chilies from the 3–6 range, using upper bounds. recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Masala
ingredients: 600 g halal boneless skinless chicken thigh, cut into 3 cm cubes
1 tbsp fresh ginger, grated, for marinade
30 g unsalted butter, for sauce base
2 tbsp fresh ginger, grated, for sauce
1 tbsp paprika, not smoked, for sauce
recipes.instructions: Coat chicken with yoghurt, marinade garlic, ginger, spices, oil, pepper and lemon juice. Refrigerate overnight or at least 3 hours. Heat searing oil over high heat; char chicken in two batches, leaving the first side for 2 minutes, then turning. Remove chicken and wipe the pan. Heat sauce oil and 30 g butter; stir onion, ginger and salt for 7 minutes. Add garlic and paprika for 2 minutes, then remaining sauce spices for 2 minutes. Add passata and water; cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes. Blend smooth, return to the pan, and stir in cream, sugar and finishing butter. Add chicken and simmer until cooked through. Serve with basmati rice.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal chicken thigh. Assume plain yoghurt, cream, butter and spice blends contain no alcohol or non-halal additives; the publisher's certification is not established.
recipes.source_notes: Uses the first listed yield, 4. Selects sweet paprika, unsalted butter and brown onion as first alternatives. Uses 2 tbsp searing oil, the upper bound. Retains optional marinade cayenne because it is not a garnish. Omits optional finishing garam masala, cilantro and suggested flatbread. recipes.title: Nasi Goreng with Chicken
ingredients: 150 g halal chicken breast, thinly sliced
3 cups cooked white rice, cold and day-old
recipes.instructions: Heat the listed oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Stir the chopped chilli and garlic through it for 10 seconds, then add the onion and cook for 1 minute. Add the sliced chicken and stir until its surface turns white. Pour in 1 tbsp kecap manis and cook for another minute, letting the chicken develop a caramelized coating. Add the cold cooked rice, remaining 2 tbsp kecap manis and shrimp paste. Stir continuously for 2 minutes so the sauce concentrates and the grains begin to caramelize; ensure the chicken is cooked through. Serve with the fried eggs, sliced green onion, tomatoes, cucumber and lime wedges.

recipes.title: Chicken Mandi with Yellow Rice
ingredients: 4 halal whole chicken legs, skin-on and bone-in
2 tbsp olive oil, divided between chicken marinade and baking
2 cups water, for steaming, with more as needed
4.5 cups reserved chicken steaming broth topped up with water
1 tbsp olive oil, for almonds and raisins
recipes.instructions: Toast whole blend spices for 2 minutes; grind and reserve 2 tsp for rice. Mix remaining blend with chicken turmeric, kosher salt and 1 tbsp olive oil; coat chicken and refrigerate overnight. Fry onions for 15 minutes, stirring every 4; leave 3 tbsp in the pot. Add reserved spices, pierced limes, bay leaves and steaming water. Steam chicken above it, covered, 50 minutes; check water every 10. Brush with remaining chicken oil; bake at 400°F for 20 minutes, then broil 5. Rinse rice; soak 10 minutes. Bloom ground saffron in hot water 5 minutes. Strain broth; top up to 4.5 cups. Boil with rice turmeric, salt and saffron; add rice, cover, cook medium-low 20 minutes; rest 10. Top with chicken, onions, oil-toasted almonds and raisins toasted 2 minutes.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal whole chicken legs. The rice liquid is broth produced by steaming that chicken, topped up with water; no purchased stock or certification is assumed.
recipes.source_notes: Keeps kosher salt as the first alternative. Retains optional saffron and dried limes because they flavor the rice. The 2 tsp rice spice mix is reserved from the homemade blend, not an additional purchase. Keeps 2 cups steaming water separate from the final 4.5 cups water-and-reserved-broth mixture; the latter reuses the former. Uses upper timing bounds of 2 minutes for spice toasting and 15 minutes for onions, stirring every 4 minutes. Omits optional parsley and suggested salad, yoghurt and Zhoug. Preserves declared cook time although the detailed stages take longer. Overnight marination is additional. No additional research was performed.

recipes.title: Iraqi Dolma
ingredients: 4 cups dry medium-grain rice, such as Calrose
3 small onions, finely diced, for filling
2 red bell peppers, finely diced, for filling
1/4 cup olive oil, for pot base
4 tbsp tomato paste, for cooking liquid
1 tsp black pepper, for cooking liquid
1/4 cup pomegranate molasses, for cooking liquid
Water, for rinsing, soaking and blanching
recipes.instructions: Mix rinsed rice with beef and all filling ingredients. Halve and hollow eggplants; scrape zucchini, cut into thirds and hollow; deseed peppers. Slit stuffing onions to their centers, microwave 1 minute, cool and separate layers. Blanch chard 3 seconds; trim stems and divide leaves. Soak grape leaves at least 1 hour, rinse and drain. Oil the pot and line with vegetable cores. Fill rigid vegetables three-quarters full; tuck stuffed onions and tightly rolled leaves around them, seams down. Mix cooking-liquid ingredients and pour halfway up the top layer. Weight with a plate, cover and boil on high 15 minutes. Remove plate, shake gently, cook medium 15 minutes, then low 1 hour until soft. Rest 15 minutes before serving.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal lean ground beef. Assume pomegranate molasses, tomato paste and jarred grape leaves contain no alcohol or non-halal additives; check product labels rather than assuming certification.
recipes.source_notes: Selects red rather than orange filling peppers, Italian rather than Indian eggplants, and microwaving rather than boiling onions. Uses upper source amounts of 4 stuffing onions and 30 grape leaves, and a 15-minute rest. Retains both Swiss chard and grape leaves. Uses olive oil for the pot base as specified in the method, while retaining the ingredient-list measure of 1/4 cup. No additional research was performed.

recipes.title: Chicken Machboos
ingredients: 4 halal whole chicken legs, skin-on and bone-in
1/2 cup vegetable oil, for the pot
1/2 tbsp vegetable oil, for toasting almonds
recipes.instructions: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Heat pot oil 1 minute; cook onions 5 minutes. Add garlic, cinnamon sticks, dried limes, bay leaves and cardamom pods for 5 minutes. Fry tomato paste 2 minutes, then simmer ground spices, salt, tomato sauce and 1 cup water for 3 minutes. Add chicken, cover and cook 20 minutes, turning halfway. Transfer chicken to a lined tray; bake 25 minutes until cooked through, then broil 2 minutes. Rinse rice and add to the pot with remaining 3.5 cups water. Cover, boil 1 minute, then cook low 20 minutes without opening; rest 5. Toast almonds in their oil until golden, within 5 minutes; remove and heat raisins 2 minutes. Fluff rice and top with chicken, almonds and raisins.
recipes.halal_notes: Use halal whole chicken legs. Select water rather than purchased broth; the chicken flavors the cooking liquid. Assume tomato products and packaged spices have no alcohol or non-halal additives.
recipes.source_notes: Selects whole chicken legs, whole dried limes, water and slivered almonds as first alternatives. Arabian Gulf identifies the dish's regional tradition; the supplied publisher metadata says only Middle Eastern and does not establish a particular country. Adds the 1/2 tbsp vegetable oil explicitly required by the source nut-toasting step as a separate ingredient. Uses upper timing bounds: chicken bakes 25 minutes and raisins cook 2 minutes. recipes.title: Musakhan Rolls
ingredients: 3 full halal chicken legs, skin on and bone in
recipes.instructions: Put the halal chicken legs, yellow onions, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cardamom pods and allspice berries in a pot, cover with water and bring to a boil, skimming off foam and topping up the water as needed. Simmer for at least 45 minutes and up to 3 hours, then lift out the chicken and shred it. Heat the oven to 400°F. Slice the red onions and cook them in the olive oil with 1 tsp salt over medium-low heat, stirring every few minutes, for about 30 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Meanwhile, toast the almonds in 1 tbsp of the olive oil over low heat. Add the chicken, sumac, ground allspice, ground cinnamon and the remaining 1 tsp salt to the onions and cook for 7 minutes, then stir in the almonds. Cut the markouk into long strips, roll about 2 tbsp filling into each and pack into an oiled 9x13-inch dish. Bake for 25 minutes, then broil for 5 minutes until crisp.
recipes.halal_notes: Uses halal chicken legs. The remaining ingredients are plant-based. Check that the packaged markouk bread contains no animal fats or non-halal additives.
recipes.source_notes: The source yields 27 rolls. The serving count is set to 9, assuming 3 rolls per person. Markouk is used because it is the bread the source names first; the Lebanese pita and tortilla substitutes are not used. The extra sumac for garnish and the yogurt served on the side are optional extras and have been omitted. The 1 tbsp of oil for toasting the almonds and the oil for the dish are taken from the cup of olive oil. Where the source gives time ranges, the upper bound is used: up to 3 hours of simmering, 30 minutes for the onions, 7 minutes for the filling and 2 tbsp of filling per roll. Water for the broth is listed because the method requires it. The source does not specify a use for the leftover broth; the strained aromatics are discarded.

recipes.title: Shish Barak (Beef Dumplings in Yogurt Sauce)
recipes.instructions: Knead the flour, warm water, 2 tbsp olive oil, sugar and 1 tsp salt into a smooth ball. This takes about 5 minutes in a mixer or 10 minutes by hand; dust with flour if the dough is sticky. Cover and rest for 30 minutes. For the filling, soften the onion in 1 tbsp olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes. Add the halal beef, 3/4 tsp salt, black pepper, sumac and seven spice and brown for 7 minutes. Fold in the pomegranate molasses and half the pine nuts, then cool. Heat the oven to 400°F. Roll the dough thin and cut 2-inch rounds. Fill each with up to 2 tsp of filling, fold into a half moon, seal, and join the ends tortellini-style. Bake for 10 minutes, then broil for 3 minutes. Whisk the cold yogurt, 1 cup water, cornstarch and 1 1/2 tsp salt until smooth. Heat over medium, whisking, for about 10 minutes until thickened; do not boil. Sizzle the garlic and cilantro in butter, whisk into the yogurt, add the dumplings and simmer for 10 minutes. Top with the remaining pine nuts.
recipes.halal_notes: Uses halal ground beef. Choose plain yogurt without gelatin and butter without non-halal additives. Check that the packaged seven spice blend and pomegranate molasses contain no alcohol-based flavourings.
recipes.source_notes: Beef is used because it is the first option; the lamb and beef mix is not used. The warm water is given as 3/4 cup and up to 1 cup, so the upper bound of 1 cup is used. The flour weight is kept; the source's approximate 3 cups is not used. The sumac is kept at 1 tbsp, the first option; the 4 tsp option is not used. Cilantro is used rather than the parsley or dried mint options. The extra cilantro for serving has been omitted as an optional garnish. The 1–2 tsp of filling per dumpling is set to the upper bound of 2 tsp. Salt and olive oil are listed separately for each section, matching the source's method. recipes.title: Moroccan Meatball Tagine in Tomato Sauce (Kefta Mkaoura)
ingredients: 1 small green bell pepper, finely chopped
recipes.instructions: Knead the halal beef with the small onion, the 3 tbsp each of parsley and cilantro, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, turmeric and cinnamon for 1–2 minutes. Roll into cherry-sized meatballs and cover. Peel, seed and chop the tomatoes. In a tagine base or skillet over medium-low heat, sauté the medium onion and green pepper in the oil for several minutes, then add the garlic for 1–2 minutes. Stir in the tomatoes, bay leaf, the 2 tbsp each of parsley and cilantro, and the remaining paprika, cumin, salt, black pepper and cayenne. Simmer covered for up to 30 minutes. Crush the tomatoes and cook covered for up to 30 minutes more, adding water as needed for a smooth sauce. Adjust the seasoning, add the meatballs and simmer covered for 15 minutes. Add the olives to heat through. Crack the eggs over the top and cook covered until the whites are firm. Garnish with parsley sprigs.
recipes.halal_notes: Uses halal ground beef. Choose jarred or brined olives packed without wine or wine vinegar. The remaining ingredients are plant-based or eggs.
recipes.source_notes: Where the source gives alternatives, the first option is used. Beef is used rather than lamb or a mix. The onion is finely chopped rather than grated. Olive oil is used rather than vegetable oil. The garlic is pressed rather than finely chopped. Cayenne is used, so the 2 chili peppers have been omitted. Parsley sprigs are used for the garnish rather than cilantro. Turmeric, cinnamon and cayenne are marked optional in the source and have been kept. The eggs and olives come from the source's optional finishing section and have also been kept; the source prefers free-range eggs. Where the source gives time ranges, the upper bound is used: 30 minutes for each simmer and 15 minutes for the meatballs. The source's total cook time is 45 minutes, so these upper bounds may run longer. The water is listed because the method adds it as needed. The meatballs and the sauce use separate portions of the same seasonings, so those ingredients are listed separately.

recipes.title: Maafe (West African Peanut Soup with Beef)
ingredients: 4 cups beef broth, reserved from boiling the beef
recipes.instructions: Season the halal beef with salt, cover with water in a large saucepan and boil until tender; the time depends on the cut. Lift out the beef and keep the broth, which should measure at least 4 cups. Heat the oil in a large pot over low heat and sauté the beef, scraping up the browned bits, then set it aside. Blend the tomatoes, half the onion, the garlic and the parsley until smooth. Sauté the remaining chopped onion in the pot for about 1 minute. Pour in the purée with the smoked paprika and white pepper and cook for 10 minutes, stirring often and adding splashes of broth to prevent burning. Add the potatoes, ground peanuts, scotch bonnet and about 3 cups of broth. Simmer for 10 minutes or more until the potatoes are tender. Return the beef, adjust the thickness with the remaining broth, and season with salt and pepper.
recipes.halal_notes: Uses halal beef. The broth is made by boiling that beef, which avoids commercial stock cubes. Choose plain ground peanuts with no additives.
recipes.source_notes: Where the source gives ranges, the upper bound is used: 2 lb beef, 4 cloves garlic, 3 tbsp parsley, 4 cups broth and 10 minutes for the purée. Where the source gives alternatives, the first option is used. Beef is used rather than chicken. Ground peanuts are used rather than peanut butter powder. A scotch bonnet is used rather than habanero or cayenne. The source lists the vegetables as potatoes, sweet potatoes, carrots and so on; potatoes, the first example, are used for the full pound. The source lists the broth as 'chicken or beef (reserved from boiling)'. Because the method makes the broth by boiling the chosen beef, it is listed as beef broth from the same pot. The source gives the oil and vegetables as minimums ('or more'); those minimum amounts are kept. The source does not specify the beef cut or pepper type. Water for boiling is listed because the method requires it.

recipes.title: Chicken Pepper Soup
ingredients: 3 1/2 lb halal chicken, cut into pieces
recipes.instructions: Put the onion, garlic, ginger, paprika, Maggi seasoning, green onions (whites and greens), parsley, scotch bonnets and njansa in a blender or food processor. Pulse until finely ground. Put the halal chicken pieces in a large pot with the blended seasoning, the bay leaf and the water. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the chicken is tender, about 45 minutes. Remove the bay leaf. Taste the broth and season with salt and white pepper. If you prefer a thinner soup, add more water and return it briefly to a simmer. Serve hot in deep bowls with plenty of the peppery broth.
recipes.halal_notes: Uses halal chicken. Maggi and other bouillon products vary in their animal-derived content, so choose a halal-certified product. Njansa and the other seasonings are plant-based.
recipes.source_notes: Where the source gives ranges, the upper bound is used: 3 1/2 lb chicken, 5 cloves garlic, 5 tbsp parsley, 3 scotch bonnets and 8 cups water. Where the source gives alternatives, the first option is used. Maggi is used rather than bouillon powder. Parsley is used rather than basil or other herbs. Scotch bonnet is used rather than habanero. The source's '1 tbsp Maggi' does not say which Maggi product is meant. The source says to purée 'the spices' without listing them; the blended mixture here is an interpretation, and the bay leaf is kept whole so it can be removed. Njansa is optional in the source and has been kept as an optional ingredient. The water amount comes from the method. The source gives about 45 minutes as its cook time and simmers until the chicken is tender. The source labels the dish as African; West African is used because the source describes it as a West African dish.
